types.description: The repository (database) of the tenant; hosts the backup methods of the bot service.

definedMethods.description: Starts a backup (dump) of the whole tenant repository and returns an operation handle. Progress and the download reference are read through runtime.operations. A dump contains all data of the tenant.

parameters.name: includeArchiveData
parameters.description: Also bundle the archive (stream data) rows of the tenant into an .octobak.zip container. Default false (MongoDB dump only).

errors.description: The dump job failed; the parameter jobId names the job, system/v1/jobs shows its error.
The dump job was interrupted (the bot service stopped while it ran) and is not started again.

definedMethods.description: Restores the tenant repository from an uploaded backup (dump .tar.gz or .octobak.zip) and returns an operation handle. The tenant database is replaced. Progress and the result are read through runtime.operations.

parameters.name: tusFileId
parameters.description: Id of the completed upload of the backup file ({tenantId}/v1/tus-upload).

parameters.name: databaseName
parameters.description: Name of the tenant database that is restored.

parameters.name: oldDatabaseName
parameters.description: Name of the database in the backup, when it differs from databaseName.

parameters.name: restoreArchiveData
parameters.description: Also restore the archive (stream data) rows of an .octobak.zip backup. Default false (MongoDB only).

errors.description: No complete, non-empty upload with this id exists for the tenant; the parameter reason says which.
The restore job failed; the parameter jobId names the job, system/v1/jobs shows its error.
The restore job was interrupted (the bot service stopped while it ran) and is not started again; the tenant database may be partly restored.

definedMethods.description: Exports the data rows of an archive of the tenant to a downloadable ZIP and returns an operation handle. Progress, the row count and the download reference are read through runtime.operations.

parameters.name: archiveRtId
parameters.description: Runtime id of the archive (System.StreamData/Archive).

parameters.name: fromUtc
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound of the exported time window (UTC). Without both bounds the whole archive is exported.

parameters.name: toUtc
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound of the exported time window (UTC).

errors.description: The export job failed (e.g. unknown archive, stream data off); the parameter jobId names the job, system/v1/jobs shows its error.
The export job was interrupted (the bot service stopped while it ran) and is not started again.

Timestamp of the LastDeploymentError. Set when LastDeploymentError is set, cleared when LastDeploymentError is cleared.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LastSuccessf.description: UTC time of the last status report that was a success (e.g. a mail poll that completed). Unlike StatusMessage it is NOT overwritten by an error report, so "last succeeded at" survives a failing streak. Empty until the first successful status report. Written by the controller's status reporting (AB#5618), which today covers pipelines only; a report counts as a success unless it is flagged as an error or its line starts with "ERROR ".

System.Communication-4.19.0/ConsecutiveS.description: Number of failed status reports since the last successful one. Incremented on every error report, reset to 0 by a successful report. Empty until the first status report. Pipelines only for now (AB#5618).

System.Communication-4.19.0/ChartName-1.description: Helm chart name within the repository (e.g. voest-app, octo-mesh-adapter).

System.Communication-4.19.0/ChartVersion.description: Helm chart version (e.g. 1.2.3). Runtime-state (AB#4706): set by the CD pipeline (UpdateWorkloadChartVersion) or the operator, not blueprint configuration - a blueprint re-apply preserves the live value instead of resetting it to the seeded version.

System.Communication-4.19.0/ValuesYaml-1.description: Full values.yaml content as a YAML string. Edited in a code editor or uploaded as a file in the Studio. Acts as the base layer of Helm values; ValueOverrides are deep-merged on top. Runtime-state (AB#4706): operator-managed, preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/Values-1.description: Structured Helm value overrides. Deep-merged on top of ValuesYaml during deploy. Entries flagged IsSecret keep their value in SecretValue (encrypted by the engine); at most one entry carrying a SecretValue per Path. Runtime-state (AB#4706): operator-managed overrides (e.g. publicUri, clientId) are preserved across blueprint re-apply; a blueprint that needs to ship NEW default overrides only seeds them on fresh installs.

System.Communication-4.19.0/ReceivesClus.description: When true, the Communication Operator injects cluster-internal credentials (MongoDB user/admin passwords, CrateDB password) into the workload's Helm release as secret-flagged value overrides. Applies to Adapters and Applications (e.g. backend services that talk to the core MongoDB / CrateDB). Defaults to false so untrusted or edge workloads do not receive cluster credentials by accident; enable only for workloads that run in the same cluster as the OctoMesh core services and need to talk to them directly. The RabbitMQ broker password is NOT controlled by this flag — it is injected unconditionally because every workload needs the controller-to-workload command bus.

System.Communication-4.19.0/IngressEnabl.description: When true, the operator projects ingress.enabled=true plus the workload Hostname into the Helm values. Cluster-wide defaults (className, cluster-issuer, TLS) come from the operator config and are not overridable per workload. Runtime-state (AB#4706): per-tenant operator decision, preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/Hostname-1.description: Public hostname used when IngressEnabled=true (e.g. adapter.staging.octo-mesh.com). Adapters get a tenant-scoped path automatically (https://<hostname>/<tenantId>); Applications use the root path. Ignored when IngressEnabled=false. Runtime-state (AB#4706): the productive hostname is tenant-specific (e.g. <tenant>.meshmakers.cloud) and operator-managed - a blueprint re-apply preserves it instead of resetting to the seeded default and silently breaking the deployed ingress/DNS.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LifecycleMod.description: Lifecycle policy of the workload (AB#4914). AlwaysOn (default) keeps it running permanently; OnDemand allows the controller to scale it to 0 replicas when idle and wake it on demand; Leased borrows a process from an adapter pool per work item (AB#4924). Runtime-state (AB#5301): an operator decision about the deployed workload, preserved across blueprint re-apply — a blueprint may seed it, but a re-apply never resets it.

System.Communication-4.19.0/IdleTimeoutM.description: Minutes without pipeline activity before an OnDemand workload is drained and scaled to 0 replicas (AB#4914). Ignored for AlwaysOn workloads. Runtime-state (AB#5301), preserved across blueprint re-apply like LifecycleMode.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LifecycleSta.description: Runtime lifecycle state of the workload (AB#4914): Running, Draining, Hibernated, or Waking. Written exclusively by the Communication Controller (idle watchdog and wake gates). Runtime-state: preserved across blueprint re-apply — resetting a Hibernated workload to Running would break the offline-is-expected semantics.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LastActivity.description: Timestamp of the last observed demand on the workload (pipeline execution, config push, or explicit wake; AB#4914). Input to the idle watchdog. Runtime-state: preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/OnDemandCapa.description: Whether the workload can safely run with LifecycleMode=OnDemand (AB#4984): true iff none of its deployed pipelines uses a process-bound trigger (e.g. FromPolling, FromWatchRtEntity) that would silently stop at 0 replicas. Computed by the Communication Controller from the registered node descriptors on adapter registration and pipeline deploy. Runtime-state: written exclusively by the controller, preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/OnDemandBloc.description: Human-readable reasons why the workload is not OnDemandCapable (AB#4984), e.g. "pipeline X uses process-bound trigger FromPolling@1". Empty when OnDemandCapable=true. Computed by the Communication Controller; shown in the Studio next to the LifecycleMode setting. Runtime-state: preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/CpuRequest-1.description: Kubernetes CPU request of the workload, e.g. "250m" (AB#7426). Optional; absent means the chart default applies. Runtime state: set by operators on live tenants and preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/CpuLimit-1.description: Kubernetes CPU limit of the workload, e.g. "1" (AB#7426). Optional; absent means the chart default applies. Runtime state, see CpuRequest.

System.Communication-4.19.0/MemoryReques.description: Kubernetes memory request of the workload, e.g. "512Mi" (AB#7426). Optional; absent means the chart default applies. Runtime state, see CpuRequest.

System.Communication-4.19.0/MemoryLimit-.description: Kubernetes memory limit of the workload, e.g. "1Gi" (AB#7426). Optional; absent means the chart default applies. Runtime state, see CpuRequest.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LastDeployme.description: Last non-fatal warning of a deployment (AB#7426), e.g. that an explicit Helm value overrides one of the typed resource settings. Written by the Communication Controller, never by an author; cleared when a deployment produces no warning. Unlike LastDeploymentError the deployment still happened.

types.description: A pool of interchangeable adapter processes owned by one tenant and leased to tenants in its subtree, one work item per lease (AB#4924). The pool declares how many members may exist (MinReplicas..MaxReplicas), how big each member is, what queue pressure starts another one, and which tenants may borrow. Members are replicas of this one workload rather than separate entities: a lease binds a member to a tenant for the duration of one work item and the member retains nothing tenant-scoped afterwards. Not to be confused with DeploymentSite, which is where a workload is deployed and which was itself called Pool before 4.0.0.

System.Communication-4.19.0/MinReplicas-.description: Lower bound on adapter pool members (AB#4924). The default of 1 is the point of the pool: one member stays hot, so the FIRST work item of the day does not pay a cold start — which is exactly the cost that makes plain OnDemand unattractive for periodic work (adapter boot 13 s, or 4.2 s with the AB#4920 warm-up). 0 is permitted and turns the pool into a scale-to-zero pool where every burst pays one cold start; choose it only where work is genuinely rare.

System.Communication-4.19.0/MaxReplicas-.description: Hard ceiling on adapter pool members (AB#4924). The pool never starts a member beyond this count no matter what the queue does — a pool that could grow without bound would reintroduce, as a cluster-capacity incident, exactly the per-tenant process sprawl this feature exists to remove. When the ceiling is reached the queue simply grows and stays visible in all three surfaces (concept §6, "Pool exhausted"): scale the pool, or move the tenant to a dedicated adapter.

System.Communication-4.19.0/PoolMemberCp.description: Kubernetes CPU request of EACH pool member, e.g. "200m" (AB#4924). One sizing per pool, applied identically to every member it starts (concept §8, Q15) — members are interchangeable by construction, so per-member sizing would have no meaning: the scheduler can hand any lease to any member. Absent means the chart default applies. A string rather than a number because Kubernetes quantities are a notation ("200m", "1", "1.5"), and re-deriving that notation from a number is how sizing bugs get introduced.
Kubernetes CPU limit of each pool member, e.g. "1" (AB#4924). See PoolMemberCpuRequest for why this is one value per pool and why it is a string.

System.Communication-4.19.0/PoolMemberMe.description: Kubernetes memory request of each pool member, e.g. "512Mi" (AB#4924). This is the number the whole feature is measured against: the prod-1 baseline in concept §1 is 170-200 Mi of pure .NET runtime per process for tenants that execute NOTHING, and a pool exists to stop paying that per tenant. Together with the lease spans (LeaseGrantedAt..LeaseReleasedAt) it is also what prices a borrower's consumption in concept §4b, so it is read for attribution and not only for scheduling.

Kubernetes memory limit of each pool member, e.g. "1Gi" (AB#4924). See PoolMemberMemoryRequest. Size it against the LARGEST tenant that may borrow the pool, not the average: a member serves one tenant at a time but serves each of them in full. AB#5330, measured: a member idles around 124 MiB and gains ~2 MiB per leased run, but the FIRST ExecuteCSharp@1 run costs it ~330 MiB permanently (the Roslyn compiler platform, loaded once per process and never released). A pool whose borrowers may run C# therefore needs at least 1Gi; at 512Mi the member is OOM-killed on the next lease it accepts, and because members are shared it takes another tenant's work down with it.

System.Communication-4.19.0/PoolScaleUpP.description: Which queue signal starts another member (AB#4924). Default QueueDepthOrWaitSeconds. Scaling is driven by the queue and never by CPU: a member waiting for a lease is I/O-bound, so its CPU utilisation carries no information about whether work is piling up behind it (concept §4a).

System.Communication-4.19.0/ScaleUpQueue.description: Number of work items waiting for a lease that makes the pool start another member, when PoolScaleUpPolicy includes the depth signal (AB#4924). Measured across the whole pool queue, not per borrowing tenant — the pool scales because IT is saturated, whereas a single tenant's burst is bounded by round-robin and LendingMaxConcurrentLeasesPerTenant instead.

How long the OLDEST waiting work item may wait before the pool starts another member, when PoolScaleUpPolicy includes the wait signal (AB#4924). Catches the case depth alone misses: two items behind one long-running lease never reach a depth threshold but can still wait for minutes. Concept §8 Q14 leaves the averaging window over which this is evaluated to be MEASURED during implementation rather than guessed, which is why the threshold is configuration and not a constant.

System.Communication-4.19.0/AdapterShari.description: Whether and to whom an adapter pool lends its members, i.e. which part of the tenant tree may be handed a lease on it (AB#4924). NotShared (default) makes the pool private to its owning tenant, which is a legitimate configuration — a pool is still useful as a way to run one tenant's own workloads elastically. The trust direction is fixed by the tenant tree and is never configurable upwards: a descendant can not lend to its ancestors (concept §3).

System.Communication-4.19.0/LendingAllow.description: Optional allow-list narrowing the tenants an adapter pool with AdapterSharingMode != NotShared lends to (AB#4924). Absent or empty means "every tenant the sharing mode resolves to". A listed tenant that the sharing mode does NOT resolve to is ignored, never granted — the allow-list is an INTERSECTION with the tenant subtree, never a way around it, so the lending scope can not be widened past the trust boundary the tenant tree establishes.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LendingMaxCo.description: Optional upper bound on how many of this pool's leases a single borrowing tenant may hold at the same time (AB#4924). Unset means no per-tenant cap — MaxReplicas and the round-robin rotation are the real bounds, which is why concept §8 Q11 deliberately left it without a default rather than inventing a number. Set it where one borrower is known to produce bursts (concept §6, "A borrowed tenant floods the queue"). It caps CONCURRENCY, not queue depth: excess work items stay Queued and visible in all three surfaces instead of being rejected.

System.Communication-4.19.0/StatusMessag.description: Human-readable status or error message from the last deployment or configuration attempt. Reflects the current/live status — overwritten on every state change including successful transitions. For persistent error history, use LastDeploymentError / LastConfigurationError.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LastDeployme.description: Last deployment error message. Set when DeploymentState transitions to Error, cleared automatically when DeploymentState transitions to Deployed. Other state transitions (Pending, Undeployed) leave this field untouched so the user can see the most recent deployment failure cause until a successful deploy resolves it.
Timestamp of the LastDeploymentError. Set when LastDeploymentError is set, cleared when LastDeploymentError is cleared.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LastSuccessf.description: UTC time of the last status report that was a success (e.g. a mail poll that completed). Unlike StatusMessage it is NOT overwritten by an error report, so "last succeeded at" survives a failing streak. Empty until the first successful status report. Written by the controller's status reporting (AB#5618), which today covers pipelines only; a report counts as a success unless it is flagged as an error or its line starts with "ERROR ".

System.Communication-4.19.0/ConsecutiveS.description: Number of failed status reports since the last successful one. Incremented on every error report, reset to 0 by a successful report. Empty until the first status report. Pipelines only for now (AB#5618).

System.Communication-4.19.0/ChartName-1.description: Helm chart name within the repository (e.g. voest-app, octo-mesh-adapter).

System.Communication-4.19.0/ChartVersion.description: Helm chart version (e.g. 1.2.3). Runtime-state (AB#4706): set by the CD pipeline (UpdateWorkloadChartVersion) or the operator, not blueprint configuration - a blueprint re-apply preserves the live value instead of resetting it to the seeded version.

System.Communication-4.19.0/ValuesYaml-1.description: Full values.yaml content as a YAML string. Edited in a code editor or uploaded as a file in the Studio. Acts as the base layer of Helm values; ValueOverrides are deep-merged on top. Runtime-state (AB#4706): operator-managed, preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/Values-1.description: Structured Helm value overrides. Deep-merged on top of ValuesYaml during deploy. Entries flagged IsSecret keep their value in SecretValue (encrypted by the engine); at most one entry carrying a SecretValue per Path. Runtime-state (AB#4706): operator-managed overrides (e.g. publicUri, clientId) are preserved across blueprint re-apply; a blueprint that needs to ship NEW default overrides only seeds them on fresh installs.

System.Communication-4.19.0/ReceivesClus.description: When true, the Communication Operator injects cluster-internal credentials (MongoDB user/admin passwords, CrateDB password) into the workload's Helm release as secret-flagged value overrides. Applies to Adapters and Applications (e.g. backend services that talk to the core MongoDB / CrateDB). Defaults to false so untrusted or edge workloads do not receive cluster credentials by accident; enable only for workloads that run in the same cluster as the OctoMesh core services and need to talk to them directly. The RabbitMQ broker password is NOT controlled by this flag — it is injected unconditionally because every workload needs the controller-to-workload command bus.

System.Communication-4.19.0/IngressEnabl.description: When true, the operator projects ingress.enabled=true plus the workload Hostname into the Helm values. Cluster-wide defaults (className, cluster-issuer, TLS) come from the operator config and are not overridable per workload. Runtime-state (AB#4706): per-tenant operator decision, preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/Hostname-1.description: Public hostname used when IngressEnabled=true (e.g. adapter.staging.octo-mesh.com). Adapters get a tenant-scoped path automatically (https://<hostname>/<tenantId>); Applications use the root path. Ignored when IngressEnabled=false. Runtime-state (AB#4706): the productive hostname is tenant-specific (e.g. <tenant>.meshmakers.cloud) and operator-managed - a blueprint re-apply preserves it instead of resetting to the seeded default and silently breaking the deployed ingress/DNS.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LifecycleMod.description: Lifecycle policy of the workload (AB#4914). AlwaysOn (default) keeps it running permanently; OnDemand allows the controller to scale it to 0 replicas when idle and wake it on demand; Leased borrows a process from an adapter pool per work item (AB#4924). Runtime-state (AB#5301): an operator decision about the deployed workload, preserved across blueprint re-apply — a blueprint may seed it, but a re-apply never resets it.

System.Communication-4.19.0/IdleTimeoutM.description: Minutes without pipeline activity before an OnDemand workload is drained and scaled to 0 replicas (AB#4914). Ignored for AlwaysOn workloads. Runtime-state (AB#5301), preserved across blueprint re-apply like LifecycleMode.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LifecycleSta.description: Runtime lifecycle state of the workload (AB#4914): Running, Draining, Hibernated, or Waking. Written exclusively by the Communication Controller (idle watchdog and wake gates). Runtime-state: preserved across blueprint re-apply — resetting a Hibernated workload to Running would break the offline-is-expected semantics.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LastActivity.description: Timestamp of the last observed demand on the workload (pipeline execution, config push, or explicit wake; AB#4914). Input to the idle watchdog. Runtime-state: preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/OnDemandCapa.description: Whether the workload can safely run with LifecycleMode=OnDemand (AB#4984): true iff none of its deployed pipelines uses a process-bound trigger (e.g. FromPolling, FromWatchRtEntity) that would silently stop at 0 replicas. Computed by the Communication Controller from the registered node descriptors on adapter registration and pipeline deploy. Runtime-state: written exclusively by the controller, preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/OnDemandBloc.description: Human-readable reasons why the workload is not OnDemandCapable (AB#4984), e.g. "pipeline X uses process-bound trigger FromPolling@1". Empty when OnDemandCapable=true. Computed by the Communication Controller; shown in the Studio next to the LifecycleMode setting. Runtime-state: preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/CpuRequest-1.description: Kubernetes CPU request of the workload, e.g. "250m" (AB#7426). Optional; absent means the chart default applies. Runtime state: set by operators on live tenants and preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/CpuLimit-1.description: Kubernetes CPU limit of the workload, e.g. "1" (AB#7426). Optional; absent means the chart default applies. Runtime state, see CpuRequest.

System.Communication-4.19.0/MemoryReques.description: Kubernetes memory request of the workload, e.g. "512Mi" (AB#7426). Optional; absent means the chart default applies. Runtime state, see CpuRequest.

System.Communication-4.19.0/MemoryLimit-.description: Kubernetes memory limit of the workload, e.g. "1Gi" (AB#7426). Optional; absent means the chart default applies. Runtime state, see CpuRequest.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LastDeployme.description: Last non-fatal warning of a deployment (AB#7426), e.g. that an explicit Helm value overrides one of the typed resource settings. Written by the Communication Controller, never by an author; cleared when a deployment produces no warning. Unlike LastDeploymentError the deployment still happened.

types.description: Configuration for AI services (e.g. Anthropic Claude API). Stores API credentials and default model settings. Referenced by pipeline nodes via ApiKeyConfigurationName.

System.Communication-4.19.0/ApiKey-1.description: API key for authenticating with an external service (e.g. Anthropic sk-ant-... key, WeClapp API token). Stored as configuration attribute, not exposed in pipeline data context.

System.Communication-4.19.0/AiModel-1.description: AI model identifier to use (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-1). Mandatory and has no default: a pinned model id goes out of date (a retired "-20250514" snapshot returns HTTP 404), so it must be set explicitly on each AiConfiguration.

System.Communication-4.19.0/Temperature-.description: Temperature for AI response generation (0.0 = deterministic, 1.0 = creative).

types.description: A tenant-specific web application deployed by the Communication Operator via Helm. Examples: energy-community, voest-app, maco-app. Most configuration (URIs, env vars, secrets) lives in ValuesYaml / Values inherited from DeployableWorkload; only operator-relevant fields are exposed as typed attributes. Ingress (IngressEnabled + Hostname) is inherited from DeployableWorkload. Optional SecretDefaults (AB#7243) declare secrets the platform provides to every tenant the application serves, never through Helm values.

definition.description: Wakes a hibernated OnDemand workload: scales it to one replica and waits until it is registered and configured (budget LifecycleWakeBudgetSeconds, default 60 s). No-op for AlwaysOn workloads, for tenants without scale-to-zero and for running workloads (REST POST Adapter/{workloadRtId}/wake).

errors.description: The workload did not reach the Configured state in the budget, or the operator could not scale it up. The wake may still complete in the cluster; retry shortly.

definition.description: Sets the Helm chart version of the workload (REST PATCH Workload/{workloadRtId}/chart-version). Empty or absent means: the newest chart of the configured repository. Does not deploy; deploy the workload afterwards.

parameters.name: chartVersion
parameters.description: A SemVer (1.2.3, 1.2.3-beta.1); empty or absent = the newest chart in the configured repository.

errors.description: The workload exists but the new chart version could not be stored.

definition.description: Deploys the workload (REST POST DeploymentSite/workloads/deploy?workloadRtId=): provisions the pipeline service account of an adapter, asks the operator of its deployment site to install or upgrade the Helm release and sets the workload Pending. The result carries a warning when an explicit Helm value overrode a typed CPU/memory setting.

errors.description: Communication is disabled for the tenant; enable it first (REST 409). Nothing was changed.
The workload could not be deployed, e.g. it is hosted by no deployment site or a Helm field is missing. Parameter message names the cause.

definition.description: Undeploys the workload (REST POST DeploymentSite/workloads/undeploy?workloadRtId=): asks the operator of its deployment site to uninstall the Helm release. Allowed while Communication is disabled, so remediation always works.

errors.description: The workload could not be undeployed, e.g. it is hosted by no deployment site or is not deployed. Parameter message names the cause.

System.Communication-4.19.0/SecretDefaul.description: Secret defaults this Application declares for every tenant it serves (AB#7243). Optional, and only on Application. Each entry is projected by the controller into a platform-owned SecretDefault entity in the Application's own tenant and its whole subtree; the target set is never widened, only narrowed by AllowedTenantIds. 🔴 This is NOT a ValueOverride: it never reaches Helm values, the pod or the app's Kubernetes Secret. Keep at most one entry per Key.

System.Communication-4.19.0/Values-1.description: Structured Helm value overrides. Deep-merged on top of ValuesYaml during deploy. Entries flagged IsSecret keep their value in SecretValue (encrypted by the engine); at most one entry carrying a SecretValue per Path. Runtime-state (AB#4706): operator-managed overrides (e.g. publicUri, clientId) are preserved across blueprint re-apply; a blueprint that needs to ship NEW default overrides only seeds them on fresh installs.

System.Communication-4.19.0/ReceivesClus.description: When true, the Communication Operator injects cluster-internal credentials (MongoDB user/admin passwords, CrateDB password) into the workload's Helm release as secret-flagged value overrides. Applies to Adapters and Applications (e.g. backend services that talk to the core MongoDB / CrateDB). Defaults to false so untrusted or edge workloads do not receive cluster credentials by accident; enable only for workloads that run in the same cluster as the OctoMesh core services and need to talk to them directly. The RabbitMQ broker password is NOT controlled by this flag — it is injected unconditionally because every workload needs the controller-to-workload command bus.

System.Communication-4.19.0/IngressEnabl.description: When true, the operator projects ingress.enabled=true plus the workload Hostname into the Helm values. Cluster-wide defaults (className, cluster-issuer, TLS) come from the operator config and are not overridable per workload. Runtime-state (AB#4706): per-tenant operator decision, preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/Hostname-1.description: Public hostname used when IngressEnabled=true (e.g. adapter.staging.octo-mesh.com). Adapters get a tenant-scoped path automatically (https://<hostname>/<tenantId>); Applications use the root path. Ignored when IngressEnabled=false. Runtime-state (AB#4706): the productive hostname is tenant-specific (e.g. <tenant>.meshmakers.cloud) and operator-managed - a blueprint re-apply preserves it instead of resetting to the seeded default and silently breaking the deployed ingress/DNS.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LifecycleMod.description: Lifecycle policy of the workload (AB#4914). AlwaysOn (default) keeps it running permanently; OnDemand allows the controller to scale it to 0 replicas when idle and wake it on demand; Leased borrows a process from an adapter pool per work item (AB#4924). Runtime-state (AB#5301): an operator decision about the deployed workload, preserved across blueprint re-apply — a blueprint may seed it, but a re-apply never resets it.

System.Communication-4.19.0/IdleTimeoutM.description: Minutes without pipeline activity before an OnDemand workload is drained and scaled to 0 replicas (AB#4914). Ignored for AlwaysOn workloads. Runtime-state (AB#5301), preserved across blueprint re-apply like LifecycleMode.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LifecycleSta.description: Runtime lifecycle state of the workload (AB#4914): Running, Draining, Hibernated, or Waking. Written exclusively by the Communication Controller (idle watchdog and wake gates). Runtime-state: preserved across blueprint re-apply — resetting a Hibernated workload to Running would break the offline-is-expected semantics.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LastActivity.description: Timestamp of the last observed demand on the workload (pipeline execution, config push, or explicit wake; AB#4914). Input to the idle watchdog. Runtime-state: preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/OnDemandCapa.description: Whether the workload can safely run with LifecycleMode=OnDemand (AB#4984): true iff none of its deployed pipelines uses a process-bound trigger (e.g. FromPolling, FromWatchRtEntity) that would silently stop at 0 replicas. Computed by the Communication Controller from the registered node descriptors on adapter registration and pipeline deploy. Runtime-state: written exclusively by the controller, preserved across blueprint re-apply.

System.Communication-4.19.0/OnDemandBloc.description: Human-readable reasons why the workload is not OnDemandCapable (AB#4984), e.g. "pipeline X uses process-bound trigger FromPolling@1". Empty when OnDemandCapable=true. Computed by the Communication Controller; shown in the Studio next to the LifecycleMode setting. Runtime-state: preserved across blueprint re-apply.

types.description: A borrower-local mirror of an AdapterPool owned by an ancestor or sibling tenant (AB#5271). Exists so a borrowing tenant can see, list and reference the pools lent to it, none of which is possible against an entity in another tenant database. Display and association only: the lease-time decision always re-reads the lending tenant's own pool, so this mirror can never widen what a borrower is allowed to use. Provisioned and kept in sync by the Communication Controller; never author-set.

System-2.8.0/Name-1.description: Unique identifier name for the entity.

System.Communication-4.19.0/Lender-1.description: The lending tenant and pool this mirror stands for (AB#5271). Single-valued: a mirror has exactly one lender. Set and cleared as one unit, so a tenant id can never be present without its pool RtId.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LentAdapterP.description: The lending pool's sharing mode as last mirrored (AB#5271). Shown so a borrower can see WHY a pool is available to it. 🔴 Display only: the lease-time decision always re-reads the lender's own pool and calls MayLendAsync, so a borrower editing this value in its own database changes what it sees, never what it may use.

Lower bound of the lending pool's replica range as last mirrored (AB#5271). Informational: it tells a borrower how much capacity is kept warm, which is what decides whether a lease is likely to be immediate or queued.
Upper bound of the lending pool's replica range as last mirrored (AB#5271). Informational, as above.

Deployment state of the lending pool as last mirrored (AB#5271). A pool that is not Deployed cannot serve a lease, so this is the one mirrored field that explains a queue that never drains. Mirrored rather than resolved on read because the borrower cannot query the lender's database.

System.Communication-4.19.0/PipelineExec.description: Scheduling class of this pipeline on a leased adapter pool (AB#4924), derived from its trigger node on save. Interactive is work a human is waiting for, Batch is everything scheduled or event-driven; within one tenant's turn in the round-robin rotation Interactive is served first, and across tenants the class has no effect at all. Default Batch: a pipeline whose trigger declares no class must never jump a queue. Computed and persisted rather than author-set, exactly like OnDemandCapable — the trigger-node descriptor contract carries the class the way it already carries RequiresRunningProcess (AB#4914 §5), so the reflection-based descriptor scan picks it up and future or third-party nodes self-describe without a controller-side list. Meaningful only for pipelines deployed to a Leased adapter; harmless and ignored everywhere else.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LastDeployme.description: Last deployment error message. Set when DeploymentState transitions to Error, cleared automatically when DeploymentState transitions to Deployed. Other state transitions (Pending, Undeployed) leave this field untouched so the user can see the most recent deployment failure cause until a successful deploy resolves it.
Timestamp of the LastDeploymentError. Set when LastDeploymentError is set, cleared when LastDeploymentError is cleared.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LastSuccessf.description: UTC time of the last status report that was a success (e.g. a mail poll that completed). Unlike StatusMessage it is NOT overwritten by an error report, so "last succeeded at" survives a failing streak. Empty until the first successful status report. Written by the controller's status reporting (AB#5618), which today covers pipelines only; a report counts as a success unless it is flagged as an error or its line starts with "ERROR ".

System.Communication-4.19.0/ConsecutiveS.description: Number of failed status reports since the last successful one. Incremented on every error report, reset to 0 by a successful report. Empty until the first status report. Pipelines only for now (AB#5618).

types.description: Records an individual pipeline execution with its status, timing, trigger type, and optional input/output data. Linked to the executed pipeline and the adapter that performed the execution. On a leased adapter pool (AB#4924) the entity exists from the moment the work item is enqueued, so one work item is one PipelineExecution from Queued through Running to completion.

System.Communication-4.19.0/ExecutionSta.description: Current status of the pipeline execution (Running, Completed, Failed, Interrupted, Cancelled).

System.Communication-4.19.0/TriggerType-.description: How this pipeline execution was initiated (Manual, Scheduled, Event, or Startup).

System.Communication-4.19.0/QueuedAt-1.description: Timestamp when the work item entered the pool queue (AB#4924). Set together with ExecutionStatus=Queued on a Leased workload and never overwritten afterwards, so QueuedAt..LeaseGrantedAt is the queue wait. Unset on a dedicated adapter, which is created Running.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LeaseGranted.description: Timestamp when a pool member was assigned this execution's tenant (AB#4924) — "when did it actually start" as opposed to "when did it stop waiting to be scheduled". Concept §8 Q5. Written on the Queued -> Running transition together with LeaseWaitMs. Unset on a dedicated adapter.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LeaseRelease.description: Timestamp when the pool member was handed back after this execution (AB#4924) — "how long did it hold the process". LeaseGrantedAt..LeaseReleasedAt is the span a member was held for one tenant, and concept §4b makes that span, multiplied by the pool's per-member sizing, the exact consumption attributed to the borrowing tenant. It is therefore a BILLING input, not only a diagnostic: it must be stamped on the release path including the TTL-expiry and crash paths, where FinishedAt may never arrive. Unset on a dedicated adapter.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LeaseWaitMs-.description: Milliseconds the work item spent waiting for a lease (AB#4924), i.e. LeaseGrantedAt - QueuedAt, written once when the lease is granted. Stored rather than derived so it survives the AB#4370 execution fold, which erases the raw execution and keeps only the statistics — without it the queue latency of a leased pool would be unmeasurable a few hours after the fact. Unset on a dedicated adapter.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LeasedFromTe.description: The lending tenant whose adapter pool served this execution (AB#4924). Written when the lease is granted. Together with LeasedFromPoolRtId it is what makes concept §4b's attribution exact: consumption is billed to the tenant whose work ran — this execution's own tenant — and the pool named here is where the per-member sizing that prices it comes from. Unset on a dedicated (AlwaysOn / OnDemand) adapter, which never leases.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LeasedFromAd.description: RtId of the AdapterPool inside LeasedFromTenantId that served this execution (AB#4924). Bare 24-character hexadecimal RtId. Recorded per execution rather than read back from the adapter's LentFromPoolRtId because the borrowing adapter can be re-pointed at a different pool later, and a cost report over past executions must reflect where the work actually ran.

System.Communication-4.19.0/LeasedOnMemb.description: Identity of the individual pool member (the process) that held the lease for this execution (AB#4924). This is what concept §5 calls "an association from the execution to the assigned member" — it can NOT be an association, because the member belongs to the lending tenant's database and this execution to the borrower's (see the file header). It is also not an RtId: members are replicas of one pool workload, not separate entities, so the value is the member's stable runtime identity (its pool-hub registration id). It exists so the per-adapter queue view — "what is this member holding, what waits behind it" — can be projected out of the pool queue.

System.Communication-4.19.0/CallerSubjec.description: Subject (sub, or client_id for a client-credentials caller) of the invoker this queued work item was created for (AB#5279). Unset when the item was queued without an invoker — a cron tick or an internal caller.

System.Communication-4.19.0/CallerTenant.description: Tenant claim of the invoker of this queued work item (AB#5279).

System.Communication-4.19.0/CallerEmail-.description: E-mail claim of the invoker of this queued work item (AB#5279).

System.Communication-4.19.0/CallerName-1.description: Display name (name / preferred_username) of the invoker of this queued work item (AB#5279).

System.Communication-4.19.0/CallerRoles-.description: Role claims of the invoker of this queued work item (AB#5279).

System.Communication-4.19.0/CallerTrustL.description: Trust the invoker established (AB#5279): 2 = strongly authenticated (bearer on the execute route), 1 = weak, 0 = none. Mirrors CallerTrustLevel of the pipeline SDK.

System.Communication-4.19.0/CallerAccess.description: The invoker's bearer token for delegation, ENCRYPTED with the controller's instance key (enc:v1: sentinel) — never plaintext (AB#5279). Written only when the controller has an encryption key; read back and decrypted at lease grant, dropped there when expired. Unset when no token was carried or no key was configured.

System.Communication-4.19.0/SealedCaller.description: Sealed (authenticated-encrypted) envelope of the invoker this queued work item was created for: principal, trust level and delegation token, bound to the tenant and to this execution (AB#7472). Written only by the controller at enqueue and re-sealed when the work item is re-queued; the controller drops it at lease grant when it does not verify. Never edit; an edited, copied or plain-text value is ignored. The token part is removed when the lease is granted.

System.Communication-4.19.0/FailureKind-.description: What a failed execution says about its writes (AB#8037): Failed (ordinary failure) or OutcomeUnknown (a write was not acknowledged and may have taken effect; a pipeline method answers METHOD_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN). Unset unless the execution failed and the adapter reported a kind.

System.Communication-4.19.0/Last30DaysSu.description: Successful executions in the last 720 UTC clock hours (30 days) including the current partial hour (= sum of the HourlyBuckets in that window; Completed = success, Failed = failure)

System.Communication-4.19.0/Last30DaysFa.description: Failed executions in the last 720 UTC clock hours (30 days) including the current partial hour (= sum of the HourlyBuckets in that window; Completed = success, Failed = failure)

System.Communication-4.19.0/LastExecutio.description: Timestamp of the most recent execution

System.Communication-4.19.0/HourlyBucket.description: Per-hour execution buckets (UTC clock hours, rolling 30 days) holding every counted execution of the hour — folded and still-retained alike. Hours before FoldedBefore are folded history; hours at or after it are recomputed from the retained executions on every statistics sweep. The 12h/24h/30d counters are exactly the sum of these buckets over the window (AB#5583).

System.Communication-4.19.0/FoldedBefore.description: Hour-aligned fold boundary (AB#5583). HourlyBuckets before this instant are folded history (their executions were deleted); buckets at or after it are a snapshot of the still-retained executions. Unset on statistics written before AB#5583.

Timestamp when a pool member was assigned this execution's tenant (AB#4924) — "when did it actually start" as opposed to "when did it stop waiting to be scheduled". Concept §8 Q5. Written on the Queued -> Running transition together with LeaseWaitMs. Unset on a dedicated adapter.

Timestamp when the pool member was handed back after this execution (AB#4924) — "how long did it hold the process". LeaseGrantedAt..LeaseReleasedAt is the span a member was held for one tenant, and concept §4b makes that span, multiplied by the pool's per-member sizing, the exact consumption attributed to the borrowing tenant. It is therefore a BILLING input, not only a diagnostic: it must be stamped on the release path including the TTL-expiry and crash paths, where FinishedAt may never arrive. Unset on a dedicated adapter.

Milliseconds the work item spent waiting for a lease (AB#4924), i.e. LeaseGrantedAt - QueuedAt, written once when the lease is granted. Stored rather than derived so it survives the AB#4370 execution fold, which erases the raw execution and keeps only the statistics — without it the queue latency of a leased pool would be unmeasurable a few hours after the fact. Unset on a dedicated adapter.

RtId of the AdapterPool inside LeasedFromTenantId that served this execution (AB#4924). Bare 24-character hexadecimal RtId. Recorded per execution rather than read back from the adapter's LentFromPoolRtId because the borrowing adapter can be re-pointed at a different pool later, and a cost report over past executions must reflect where the work actually ran.

The lending tenant whose adapter pool served this execution (AB#4924). Written when the lease is granted. Together with LeasedFromPoolRtId it is what makes concept §4b's attribution exact: consumption is billed to the tenant whose work ran — this execution's own tenant — and the pool named here is where the per-member sizing that prices it comes from. Unset on a dedicated (AlwaysOn / OnDemand) adapter, which never leases.

Identity of the individual pool member (the process) that held the lease for this execution (AB#4924). This is what concept §5 calls "an association from the execution to the assigned member" — it can NOT be an association, because the member belongs to the lending tenant's database and this execution to the borrower's (see the file header). It is also not an RtId: members are replicas of one pool workload, not separate entities, so the value is the member's stable runtime identity (its pool-hub registration id). It exists so the per-adapter queue view — "what is this member holding, what waits behind it" — can be projected out of the pool queue.
The lending tenant and pool this mirror stands for (AB#5271). Single-valued: a mirror has exactly one lender. Set and cleared as one unit, so a tenant id can never be present without its pool RtId.

Member of the LenderReference record (AB#5271): the bare 24-character hexadecimal RtId of the AdapterPool inside LenderTenantId. Names the POOL, never an individual member — membership is elastic, so a reference to a member would dangle the moment that member is drained.

Member of the LenderReference record (AB#5271): the tenant that owns the lent AdapterPool. Mirrored from the lending side; never author-set. The controller re-resolves it on every lease, so a stale value produces a refused deploy with a named reason rather than a wrong grant.

Optional allow-list narrowing the tenants an adapter pool with AdapterSharingMode != NotShared lends to (AB#4924). Absent or empty means "every tenant the sharing mode resolves to". A listed tenant that the sharing mode does NOT resolve to is ignored, never granted — the allow-list is an INTERSECTION with the tenant subtree, never a way around it, so the lending scope can not be widened past the trust boundary the tenant tree establishes.

Optional upper bound on how many of this pool's leases a single borrowing tenant may hold at the same time (AB#4924). Unset means no per-tenant cap — MaxReplicas and the round-robin rotation are the real bounds, which is why concept §8 Q11 deliberately left it without a default rather than inventing a number. Set it where one borrower is known to produce bursts (concept §6, "A borrowed tenant floods the queue"). It caps CONCURRENCY, not queue depth: excess work items stay Queued and visible in all three surfaces instead of being rejected.

Deployment state of the lending pool as last mirrored (AB#5271). A pool that is not Deployed cannot serve a lease, so this is the one mirrored field that explains a queue that never drains. Mirrored rather than resolved on read because the borrower cannot query the lender's database.
Upper bound of the lending pool's replica range as last mirrored (AB#5271). Informational, as above.

Scheduling class of this pipeline on a leased adapter pool (AB#4924), derived from its trigger node on save. Interactive is work a human is waiting for, Batch is everything scheduled or event-driven; within one tenant's turn in the round-robin rotation Interactive is served first, and across tenants the class has no effect at all. Default Batch: a pipeline whose trigger declares no class must never jump a queue. Computed and persisted rather than author-set, exactly like OnDemandCapable — the trigger-node descriptor contract carries the class the way it already carries RequiresRunningProcess (AB#4914 §5), so the reflection-based descriptor scan picks it up and future or third-party nodes self-describe without a controller-side list. Kubernetes CPU limit of each pool member, e.g. "1" (AB#4924). See PoolMemberCpuRequest for why this is one value per pool and why it is a string.

Kubernetes CPU request of EACH pool member, e.g. "200m" (AB#4924). One sizing per pool, applied identically to every member it starts (concept §8, Q15) — members are interchangeable by construction, so per-member sizing would have no meaning: the scheduler can hand any lease to any member. Absent means the chart default applies. A string rather than a number because Kubernetes quantities are a notation ("200m", "1", "1.5"), and re-deriving that notation from a number is how sizing bugs get introduced.

Kubernetes memory limit of each pool member, e.g. "1Gi" (AB#4924). See PoolMemberMemoryRequest. Size it against the LARGEST tenant that may borrow the pool, not the average: a member serves one tenant at a time but serves each of them in full. AB#5330, measured: a member idles around 124 MiB and gains ~2 MiB per leased run, but the FIRST ExecuteCSharp@1 run costs it ~330 MiB permanently (the Roslyn compiler platform, loaded once per process and never released). A pool whose borrowers may run C# therefore needs at least 1Gi; at 512Mi the member is OOM-killed on the next lease it accepts, and because members are shared it takes another tenant's work down with it.

Kubernetes memory request of each pool member, e.g. "512Mi" (AB#4924). This is the number the whole feature is measured against: the prod-1 baseline in concept §1 is 170-200 Mi of pure .NET runtime per process for tenants that execute NOTHING, and a pool exists to stop paying that per tenant. Together with the lease spans (LeaseGrantedAt..LeaseReleasedAt) it is also what prices a borrower's consumption in concept §4b, so it is read for attribution and not only for scheduling.

Which queue signal starts another member (AB#4924). Default QueueDepthOrWaitSeconds. Scaling is driven by the queue and never by CPU: a member waiting for a lease is I/O-bound, so its CPU utilisation carries no information about whether work is piling up behind it (concept §4a).

Number of work items waiting for a lease that makes the pool start another member, when PoolScaleUpPolicy includes the depth signal (AB#4924). Measured across the whole pool queue, not per borrowing tenant — the pool scales because IT is saturated, whereas a single tenant's burst is bounded by round-robin and LendingMaxConcurrentLeasesPerTenant instead.

How long the OLDEST waiting work item may wait before the pool starts another member, when PoolScaleUpPolicy includes the wait signal (AB#4924). Catches the case depth alone misses: two items behind one long-running lease never reach a depth threshold but can still wait for minutes. Concept §8 Q14 leaves the averaging window over which this is evaluated to be MEASURED during implementation rather than guessed, which is why the threshold is configuration and not a constant.

Sealed (authenticated-encrypted) envelope of the invoker this queued work item was created for: principal, trust level and delegation token, bound to the tenant and to this execution (AB#7472). Never edit; an edited, copied or plain-text value is ignored. The token part is removed when the lease is granted.

Whether and to whom an adapter lends its process as a leasable pool member (AB#4924). NotShared (default) keeps the adapter private to its own tenant — the behaviour of every adapter in the estate today. Descendants lends to any descendant of the owning tenant, direct or indirect, resolved by the same breadth-first tenant walk as GET {tenantId}/v1/tenants/descendants (AB#5151). DescendantsAndSiblings additionally lends to tenants that share the owning tenant's parent. In every mode the optional LendingAllowedTenantIds allow-list narrows the resolved set further; it never widens it, so a tenant outside the subtree can not be granted a lease by listing it.
Indicates the current SignalR connection state of an adapter or pool operator.
Indicates whether a deployable entity has been successfully configured with its pipeline definitions and settings.

Tracks whether a deployable entity (adapter, application, pipeline, pool, or trigger) is currently deployed and active. Disabled means the entity cannot be deployed at all: Edge pools (no central operator CR), workloads missing Helm chart/version/repository, or pipelines/triggers whose adapter is Disabled. Deploy/Undeploy actions are rejected on Disabled entities.

Where a pool's adapter workloads are hosted. Cloud pools are auto-deployed by the central Communication Operator into the OctoMesh cluster; Edge pools must be installed and run by an external operator outside the central cluster.
Distribution channel of a Helm chart repository. Used as a label so the UI can colour-code dev vs release sources; the operator does not derive behavior from this value.

Which kind of chart a Helm repository serves. Adapters covers adapter and platform charts, Applications covers tenant-app charts. Used by the Communication Controller to pick a repository for a workload that carries no explicit HelmRepository association; never a label only.

Author-configured lifecycle policy of a deployable workload. AlwaysOn (default) keeps the workload running permanently. OnDemand lets the controller scale it to 0 replicas when idle and wake it on demand (AB#4914); only valid for workloads whose deployed pipelines use exclusively wake-capable triggers. Auto is reserved for a future controller-decided mode and is rejected by validation until implemented. Leased (AB#4924) means the workload has no process of its own at all: its pipelines execute on an AdapterPool lent by an ancestor or sibling tenant, one lease per work item — see the LentFrom association to a LentAdapterPool mirror (AB#5271) and docs/concepts/shared-adapter-leasing.md. Leased is the BORROWER's mode and only ever that; an AdapterPool is its own workload type with a replica range and is not itself Leased.

Runtime lifecycle state of an OnDemand workload (AB#4914). Running: normal operation. Draining: idle timeout reached, scale-to-0 requested. Hibernated: scaled to 0 replicas on purpose — CommunicationState=Offline is expected and must not raise alarms. Waking: a demand signal triggered scale-to-1; consumers wait for ConfigurationState=Configured. AlwaysOn workloads stay Running permanently.

Scheduling class of a pipeline on a leased adapter pool (AB#4924), resolved from the pipeline's trigger node when the pipeline is SAVED and persisted here — not parsed from the YAML at dequeue time, so the scheduler reads a field and the Studio / octo-cli / MCP surfaces can show WHY a job sits where it does. Interactive is work a human is waiting for (HTTP request, manual run, Studio "execute now"). Batch is everything scheduled or event-driven. Within one tenant's turn in the round-robin rotation, Interactive is served before Batch; across tenants the class has no effect whatsoever. Mirrors OnDemandCapable: computed, persisted for display, and re-resolved whenever the pipeline is saved — so a pipeline edited to a different trigger changes class visibly, as a change, rather than as behaviour that quietly shifts.

What a failed pipeline execution says about its writes (AB#8037). Failed is an ordinary failure (the database refused the write, or the pipeline failed for another reason). OutcomeUnknown means a write was neither acknowledged nor refused (MongoDB write-concern error, UnknownTransactionCommitResult) and may have taken effect; a pipeline method then answers METHOD_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN with a correlation id instead of METHOD_HANDLER_FAILED. Unset on a successful execution and on executions reported by an adapter that predates the field (treated as Failed).

Status of a pipeline execution lifecycle, from queued or running through completion or failure. Queued (AB#4924) precedes Running on a Leased workload: the execution entity exists from the moment the work item is enqueued, so one execution stays one entity from enqueue to completion and the Studio renders a continuous history instead of joining a queue and an execution source.
Indicates how a pipeline execution was initiated.

Which queue signal makes an adapter pool start another member (AB#4924). QueueDepth scales when the number of work items waiting for a lease crosses ScaleUpQueueDepthThreshold. QueueWaitSeconds scales when the oldest waiting item has waited longer than ScaleUpQueueWaitSeconds. QueueDepthOrWaitSeconds (default) scales on whichever fires first, which is the behaviour a pool wants in practice: depth catches a burst, wait time catches a slow trickle behind one long-running lease. CPU-based scaling is deliberately absent — a member waiting for a lease is idle by construction.

Audited action of a Signal channel registration attempt (AB#5143). Every register/verify/delete attempt against the tenant's SignalChannel — including failed ones — appends one entry with this action to the channel's RegistrationHistory. Adopted means the bridge already held a working account for the number, so register/verify were skipped and the definition went straight to Registered. ProfileUpdated records a display-name profile push (PUT /v1/profiles/{number}) — its detail carries the pushed name, the failure text for a rejected push on the displayName endpoint, or the cleared note (clearing never touches the bridge profile). Deleted is part of the audit vocabulary but a persisted Deleted entry never survives: a successful DELETE erases the definition including its history (fresh definition = fresh history); the system event trail still records the deletion.

Registration state of a tenant's Signal phone number against the Signal bridge (AB#5143). Unregistered means a definition exists but no registration was started (or a rate-limited attempt is pending retry). CodePending means the bridge accepted the register call and Signal sent an SMS verification code. Registered means the verify call succeeded and the number can send/receive. Failed means the last register attempt was rejected by the bridge (see LastError); a new register attempt is allowed.
